title: Knowledge Check 1: Lessons 1–5
description: Pooled check over Lessons 1–5 of the Hermes Consultant Intermediate series. Score 80% or higher to unlock the cert prep exam.

This lesson teaches all three.

This lesson is about the harder move, the one that separates a practitioner who delivers engagements from one who builds a practice.
You now have one system that runs without you in the room.

questions.question: Per the lesson “Complex Client Environments: Existing Stacks, Enterprise Constraints, and Sandboxed Deploys”, what is the central focus?
options: The clean single-client world where you chose the stack is the exception, not the rule. This lesson teaches you to land a packaged agent delivery inside a compa…

A review of unrelated productivity tools

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: The clean single-client world where you chose the stack is the exception, not the rule. This lesson teaches you to land a packaged agent delivery inside a company that already has infrastructure, security rules, and processes you did not choose, and to keep the toolkit working when the environment fights back.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: Lesson 4 gave you the toolkit: packaged, trigger-first skills that let the next engagement start from a running start instead of a blank page.
The engagements so far, even the ones hardened for production, all happened in a world where you had a clean runway: you chose the data sources, the model, the guardrail set, the environment.
This lesson is about what happens when you bring that toolkit into a company that already exists.

Most real work happens inside infrastructure, security rules, and processes you did not choose, and it happens inside a stack that was running before you arrived and will keep running after you leave.
questions.explanation: Lesson 4 gave you the toolkit: packaged, trigger-first skills that let the next engagement start from a running start instead of a blank page.
